props.title: The Other

sections.content: The Other stands as a masterpiece of psychological horror that influenced countless evil child films. Director Robert Mulligan (who directed To Kill a Mockingbird (1962)) crafts a haunting tale of twin brothers in 1930s Connecticut that plays like a rural American gothic nightmare. The film pioneered techniques later seen in The Omen (1976) and The Good Son (1993), using child actors to create genuine menace. Tom Tryon adapted his own novel, bringing a literary depth rarely seen in 1970s horror.

movies.slug: Gothic horror about a governess caring for two potentially possessed children

sections.content: The film's exploration of rural Americana and childhood corruption found echoes in later works like Pet Sematary (1989) and Children of the Corn (1984). Its period setting and focus on family dynamics created a template for psychological horror that emphasizes atmosphere over gore. The performances by Chris and Martin Udvarnoky as the twins Niles and Holland Perry remain among the most convincing child performances in horror cinema.

The film's influence extends beyond evil child narratives into broader psychological horror. Its techniques for suggesting supernatural elements while maintaining ambiguity influenced films like The Changeling (1980) and The Others (2001). The way it uses bright summer settings to create unease predates similar approaches in Midsommar (2019). SUBHEAD: Rural Gothic and Family Horror

sections.content: The Other helped establish rural gothic as a distinct horror subset, alongside films like The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974). Its portrayal of family secrets and generational trauma in an idyllic setting influenced works like Hereditary (2018) and The Dark and the Wicked (2020). The film's use of childhood games and seemingly innocent activities turned sinister became a horror staple.
